claim: GNR-710 has a core size of 60.0 ± 7.5 nm by 25.7 ± 3.7 nm with an average aspect ratio of 2.3 ± 0.3.
source: The first batch consisted of GNRs with a longitudinal surface plasmon resonance (LSPR) peak at 710 nm (GNR-710). Their core size was 60.0 ± 7.5 nm by 25.7 ± 3.7 nm with an average aspect ratio of 2.3 ± 0.3.
evidence: The manuscript provides specific measurements of GNR-710 dimensions obtained from experimental characterization.

claim: GNR-860 has a core size of 93.8 ± 9.3 nm by 25.2 ± 4.4 nm with an average aspect ratio of 3.8 ± 0.5.
source: The second batch had a LSPR peak at 860 nm (GNR-860). In this case, their size was 93.8 ± 9.3 nm by 25.2 ± 4.4 nm with an average aspect ratio of 3.8 ± 0.5)
evidence: The manuscript provides specific measurements of GNR-860 dimensions obtained from experimental characterization.

claim: Both GNR batches were prepared to have LSPR bands in the NIR to favor their detection deep inside tissues.
source: Both GNRs were prepared to have LSPR bands in the NIR to favour their detection deep inside tissues.
evidence: This is a design rationale stated by the authors based on known optical properties of NIR wavelengths in tissue.

claim: A 35 nm silica shell is needed to minimize plasmon coupling between GNRs after cell uptake.
source: We have recently demonstrated that a 35 nm silica shell is needed to minimise plasmon coupling between GNRs after cell uptake (Comenge et al., 2016).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to previous work by the authors.

claim: GNR-710 has a silica shell thickness of 38.7 ± 1.9 nm.
source: Specifically, GNR-710 and GNRs-860 nm have a silica shell thickness of 38.7 ± 1.9 nm and 35.7 ± 1.6 nm, respectively (Figure 1a).
evidence: The manuscript provides specific measurements of silica shell thickness and references Figure 1a showing TEM images.

claim: GNR-860 has a silica shell thickness of 35.7 ± 1.6 nm.
source: Specifically, GNR-710 and GNRs-860 nm have a silica shell thickness of 38.7 ± 1.9 nm and 35.7 ± 1.6 nm, respectively (Figure 1a).
evidence: The manuscript provides specific measurements of silica shell thickness and references Figure 1a showing TEM images.

claim: The murine MSC line has the capability to differentiate into mesenchymal derivatives but can also form tumours occasionally.
source: A murine MSC line was selected for labelling and tracking, since these cells have the capability to differentiate into mesenchymal derivatives, but can also form tumours occasionally (Comenge et al., 2016; Kuzma-Kuzniarska et al., 2012).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: O.D. = 4 corresponds to approximately 100 pM GNR-710.
source: For reference, O.D. = 4 corresponds to ~100 pM GNR-710 and ~72.5 pM GNR-860 (calculated by relating the absorbance at 400 nm of GNRs before silica coating to concentrations of molecular gold) (Pastoriza-Santos and Liz-Marzán, 2013).
evidence: This is a calculated value based on absorbance measurements and a cited method.

claim: O.D. = 4 corresponds to approximately 72.5 pM GNR-860.
source: For reference, O.D. = 4 corresponds to ~100 pM GNR-710 and ~72.5 pM GNR-860 (calculated by relating the absorbance at 400 nm of GNRs before silica coating to concentrations of molecular gold) (Pastoriza-Santos and Liz-Marzán, 2013).
evidence: This is a calculated value based on absorbance measurements and a cited method.

claim: GNRs are localized inside vesicles after cell uptake, with silica shells separating the gold cores.
source: TEM images of cells show GNRs localised inside vesicles, with silica shells separating the gold cores (Figure 1b, and Figure 1—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is directly observed in TEM images presented in the manuscript.

claim: The optical properties of GNRs were largely preserved after cell uptake.
source: In line with our previous report, the optical properties of GNRs were largely preserved after cell uptake (Figure 1c,d).
evidence: This is demonstrated by spectroscopic data shown in Figure 1c,d and is consistent with previous work.

claim: Preservation of the absorbance intensity and the shape of the plasmon band are prerequisite for optimal photoacoustic detection of GNR-labelled cells.
source: Preservation of the absorbance intensity and the shape of the plasmon band are prerequisite for an optimal photoacoustic detection of GNR-labelled cells since it relies on a spectral deconvolution to differentiate intrinsic absorbers from probes.
evidence: This is a technical explanation based on the principles of photoacoustic imaging and spectral unmixing.

claim: At the highest GNR concentration (O.D. = 4), cell viability was 92.0 ± 2.6% for GNR-710 and 91.7 ± 1.6% for GNR-860.
source: Only at the highest GNR concentration was a slight decrease in cell viability observed: 92.0 ± 2.6% and 91.7 ± 1.6% for GNR-710 and GNR-860, respectively.
evidence: This is experimental data from cell viability assays shown in Figure 1e.

claim: Silica-coated GNRs did not affect cell viability, proliferation or differentiation potential of the mMSCs.
source: These results are in agreement with our previous work, in which we showed that silica-coated GNRs did not affect cell viability, proliferation or differentiation potential of the mMSCs (Comenge et al., 2016).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to previous work and is consistent with current experimental results.

claim: Bi-cistronic lentivirus vectors were generated for expression of firefly luciferase and iRFP720 from the general eukaryotic EF1α promoter.
source: To combine the sensitivity of bioluminescence imaging with the spatial resolution of MSOT, we generated bi-cistronic lentivirus vectors for expression of firefly luciferase and iRFP720 from the general eukaryotic EF1α promoter (Figure 2a).
evidence: This describes the experimental design and construction of the vectors shown in Figure 2a.

claim: The E2A-vector-transfected cells showed a five times higher luciferase bioluminescence compared to IRES-vector-transfected cells.
source: For both types of reporter cells (IRES-vector and E2A-vector transfected), the fluorescence signal intensity for iRFP720 was the same, but the E2A-vector-transfected cells showed a five times higher luciferase bioluminescence (Figure 2d,e).
evidence: This is quantitative data from IVIS Spectrum imaging comparing the two vector types.

claim: A superior translation efficiency of the second ORF from a single mRNA was achieved via an E2A element as compared to an IRES element.
source: These data indicate that in the context of our bi-cistronic lentivirus vectors, a superior translation efficiency of the second ORF from a single mRNA was achieved via an E2A element as compared to an IRES element.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the experimental data comparing IRES and E2A vectors.

claim: In contrast to luciferase, iRFP720 was preferentially localized in the nucleus.
source: Co-expression of iRFP720 and luciferase in individual cells was confirmed by immunocytochemistry (Figure 2c), which also indicated that, in contrast to luciferase, iRFP720 was preferentially localised in the nucleus.
evidence: This is observed in immunocytochemistry images shown in Figure 2c.

claim: 1.5 × 10^6 mMSCs transduced with the iRFP720-E2A-Luc lentivirus and labelled with GNRs were administered via ultrasound-guided intracardiac injection into the left ventricle.
source: Specifically, 1.5 × 106 mMSCs transduced with the iRFP720-E2A-Luc lentivirus and labelled with GNRs were administered via ultrasound-guided intracardiac injection into the left ventricle.
evidence: This describes the experimental procedure for cell administration.

claim: Left ventricle administration was chosen for cells to enter the arterial circulation rather than the venous.
source: Left ventricle administration was chosen for cells to enter the arterial circulation rather than the venous.
evidence: This is a methodological choice explained by the authors.

claim: Left ventricle administration allows cells to pass through all organs before returning to the right ventricle and subsequently lungs, where they become sequestered in the pulmonary microvasculature.
source: This allows cells to pass through all organs before returning to the right ventricle and subsequently lungs, where they become sequestered in the pulmonary microvasculature (Kean et al., 2013; Fischer et al., 2009).
evidence: This is a known physiological outcome supported by citations.

claim: Bioluminescence imaging provides excellent sensitivity but its anatomical resolution is poor, mainly due to the high scattering of photons by tissue.
source: While bioluminescence imaging provides excellent sensitivity, its anatomical resolution is poor, mainly due to the high scattering of photons by tissue (Patterson et al., 1989; Ntziachristos et al., 2005).
evidence: This is a known limitation of bioluminescence imaging supported by citations.

claim: Photoacoustic imaging provides superior spatial resolution (150 µm in the system used).
source: By contrast, photoacoustic imaging provides superior spatial resolution (150 µm in our system) (Ntziachristos and Razansky, 2010).
evidence: This is a technical specification of the imaging system used, supported by citation.

claim: Cell localization in the head, liver and kidney regions was clearly observed with both bioluminescence and MSOT imaging modalities.
source: Cell localisation in the head, liver and kidney regions was clearly observed with both imaging modalities (Figure 3a,b), and the cell presence within organs was confirmed in the photoacoustic scans through the respective regions (Figure 3c).
evidence: This is demonstrated by imaging data shown in Figure 3.

claim: The distribution pattern after intracardiac injection is in agreement with other, different types of assessments in previous reports.
source: This distribution is in agreement with other, different types of assessments in previous reports (Basse et al., 1988).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to previous work.

claim: The presence of cells in the brain region is probably due to cell trapping in small capillaries.
source: The presence of cells in the brain region is probably due to cell trapping in small capillaries, as reported also in other studies after intracardiac injection of cells (Heyn et al., 2006).
evidence: This is an interpretation supported by citation to similar observations in other studies.

claim: The mMSCs remain in the lumen of the brain capillaries and do not cross the blood-brain barrier.
source: As shown in our parallel work (Scarfe et al., 2017), the mMSCs remain in the lumen of the brain capillaries and do not cross the blood-brain barrier.
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to parallel work by the authors.

claim: There was no difference in the bioluminescence signal biodistribution when cells with or without gold nanorods were injected.
source: It should be noted here that there was no difference in the bioluminescence signal biodistribution when cells with or without gold nanorods were injected, indicating that GNR uptake does not affect the overall behaviour of the cells (Figure 3—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is demonstrated by comparative imaging data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1.

claim: GNR uptake does not affect the overall behaviour of the cells.
source: It should be noted here that there was no difference in the bioluminescence signal biodistribution when cells with or without gold nanorods were injected, indicating that GNR uptake does not affect the overall behaviour of the cells (Figure 3—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is inferred from the observation that biodistribution patterns are the same with or without GNRs.

claim: When the 'wrong' spectrum was applied (i.e. the GNR-710 spectrum to an animal injected with GNR-860-labelled cells, and vice versa), no GNR-specific signals were detected in photoacoustic images pre- and post-injection.
source: Second, when we applied the unmixing algorithm with the 'wrong' spectrum (i.e. the GNR-710 spectrum to an animal injected with GNR-860-labelled cells, and vice versa), no GNR-specific signals were detected in photoacoustic images pre- and post-injection (Figure 4).
evidence: This is a control experiment demonstrating specificity of the signal, shown in Figure 4.

claim: An increase in the photoacoustic intensity was only observed in the range of wavelengths in which corresponding GNRs have the higher absorbance.
source: Third, when the photoacoustic spectra of regions of interest before and after injection of cells were extracted, an increase in the photoacoustic intensity was only observed in the range of wavelengths in which corresponding GNRs have the higher absorbance, while intensity in the other wavelengths remained similar (Figure 4—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is demonstrated by spectral analysis shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 1.

claim: The photoacoustic signal provided by iRFP720 expression was not strong enough to detect the cells immediately after injection by means of photoacoustic imaging.
source: As expected, the photoacoustic signal provided by iRFP720 expression was not strong enough to detect the cells immediately after injection by means of photoacoustic imaging (Figure 4).
evidence: This is an observation from the imaging data shown in Figure 4.

claim: One day after GNR-labelled cell infusion, only between 15–22% of the initial bioluminescence signal in whole mice persisted.
source: One day after GNR-labelled cell infusion, only between 15–22% of the initial bioluminescence signal in whole mice persisted (Figure 5b), decreasing to less than 4% by day 5.
evidence: This is quantitative data from bioluminescence imaging shown in Figure 5b.

claim: By day 5 after cell infusion, less than 4% of the initial bioluminescence signal persisted.
source: One day after GNR-labelled cell infusion, only between 15–22% of the initial bioluminescence signal in whole mice persisted (Figure 5b), decreasing to less than 4% by day 5.
evidence: This is quantitative data from bioluminescence imaging shown in Figure 5b.

claim: Substantial amounts of cell death following cell infusion were expected from previous reports.
source: Such substantial amounts of cell death following cell infusion were expected from previous reports (Tögel et al., 2008; Bentzon et al., 2005).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: A similar degree of cell death was observed with cells not labelled with GNRs, indicating that cell loss in vivo was not caused by GNR labelling.
source: A similar degree of cell death was observed with cells not labelled with GNRs, indicating that cell loss in vivo was not caused by GNR labelling (Figure 5—source data 1).
evidence: This is demonstrated by comparative data showing similar cell death rates with and without GNR labelling.

claim: After 24 hr, the bioluminescence signal and the photoacoustic signal for GNRs were no longer localized in the same regions/organs.
source: Interestingly, after 24 hr, the bioluminescence signal and the photoacoustic signal for GNRs were no longer localised in the same regions/organs (Figure 5a–c), indicating that the vast majority of GNRs followed a different fate than the remaining luciferase-expressing cells.
evidence: This is observed in the imaging data shown in Figure 5a-c.

claim: The vast majority of GNRs followed a different fate than the remaining luciferase-expressing cells.
source: Interestingly, after 24 hr, the bioluminescence signal and the photoacoustic signal for GNRs were no longer localised in the same regions/organs (Figure 5a–c), indicating that the vast majority of GNRs followed a different fate than the remaining luciferase-expressing cells.
evidence: This is inferred from the observation that GNR and bioluminescence signals are in different locations after 24 hours.

claim: The MSOT signal for GNR-860 increased dramatically in the liver over 24 hours.
source: By contrast, the MSOT signal for GNR-860 increased dramatically in the liver over the same timescale, but was substantially reduced in regions such as the kidneys and head where it had been predominant immediately after cell injection (Figure 5a,c).
evidence: This is observed in the MSOT imaging data shown in Figure 5a,c.

claim: The MSOT signal for GNR-860 was substantially reduced in regions such as the kidneys and head where it had been predominant immediately after cell injection.
source: By contrast, the MSOT signal for GNR-860 increased dramatically in the liver over the same timescale, but was substantially reduced in regions such as the kidneys and head where it had been predominant immediately after cell injection (Figure 5a,c).
evidence: This is observed in the MSOT imaging data shown in Figure 5a,c.

claim: Photoacoustic signal can be produced from GNRs independently, irrespective of whether they are within cells, or if the cells are viable.
source: Whilst luminescent signal is based on living cells, photoacoustic signal can be produced from GNRs independently, irrespective of whether they are within cells, or if the cells are viable.
evidence: This is a fundamental property of the two imaging modalities based on their mechanisms.

claim: The liver plays an important role in the clearance of GNRs and potentially associated cell debris following the massive loss of cells during the first 24 hr after injection.
source: Thus, these data suggest that the liver plays an important role in the clearance of GNRs and potentially associated cell debris following the massive loss of cells during the first 24 hr after injection, as previously reported (Eggenhofer et al., 2012; Khabbal et al., 2015).
evidence: This is inferred from the imaging data and supported by citations to previous reports.

claim: These findings are in line with reports describing nanoparticle clearance through the hepato-biliary tract.
source: In addition, these findings are in line with reports describing nanoparticle clearance through the hepato-biliary tract (Longmire et al., 2008; Hirn et al., 2011; Lankveld et al., 2011).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous studies on nanoparticle clearance.

claim: The photoacoustic signal in the liver dropped by 47% after 5 days.
source: We observed that the clearance could be continuously monitored in a longitudinal fashion since the photoacoustic signal in the liver dropped by 47% after 5 days and by 73% after 25 days (Figure 5d).
evidence: This is quantitative data from longitudinal MSOT imaging shown in Figure 5d.

claim: The photoacoustic signal in the liver dropped by 73% after 25 days.
source: We observed that the clearance could be continuously monitored in a longitudinal fashion since the photoacoustic signal in the liver dropped by 47% after 5 days and by 73% after 25 days (Figure 5d).
evidence: This is quantitative data from longitudinal MSOT imaging shown in Figure 5d.

claim: By day 5, cells were no longer detectable by BLI in the regions where they had first accumulated (i.e. brain, kidneys and spinal cord).
source: Following the substantial loss in cell viability over the first 24 hr, signal intensity declined further and by day 5 cells were no longer detectable by BLI in the regions where they had first accumulated (i.e. brain, kidneys and spinal cord, Figure 3).
evidence: This is observed in the bioluminescence imaging data.

claim: BLI signals from cells that had settled in different locations were observed after day 5.
source: However, we now observed BLI signals from cells that had settled in different locations (Figure 6—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is observed in the bioluminescence imaging data shown in Figure 6—figure supplement 1.

claim: The signal intensity increased over the following weeks as cells grew into tumours.
source: The signal intensity increased over the following weeks as cells grew into tumours (Figure 6—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is observed in longitudinal bioluminescence imaging data shown in Figure 6—figure supplement 1.

claim: The mMSC cell line had been reported to form osteoid structures in vivo.
source: Since the mMSC cell line had been reported to form osteoid structures in vivo (Kuzma-Kuzniarska et al., 2012), and recent results from our group have revealed the capacity of the cells to form osteosarcomas (Scarfe et al., 2017), we anticipated the possibility of tumour development.
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to a previous study.

claim: Recent results from the authors' group have revealed the capacity of the cells to form osteosarcomas.
source: Since the mMSC cell line had been reported to form osteoid structures in vivo (Kuzma-Kuzniarska et al., 2012), and recent results from our group have revealed the capacity of the cells to form osteosarcomas (Scarfe et al., 2017), we anticipated the possibility of tumour development.
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to recent work by the authors.

claim: Bioluminescence is limited by the poor spatial resolution at depths beyond 1 mm due to photon scattering.
source: However, bioluminescence is limited by the poor spatial resolution at depths beyond 1 mm due to photon scattering.
evidence: This is a known limitation of bioluminescence imaging based on the physics of light scattering in tissue.

claim: Presence of iRFP720 resulted in a change of the photoacoustic spectra in the regions where cells were forming tumours.
source: Presence of iRFP720 resulted in a change of the photoacoustic spectra in the regions where cells were forming tumours (Figure 6, and Figure 6—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This is demonstrated by spectral analysis shown in Figure 6 and Figure 6—figure supplement 2.

claim: The iRFP720 absorption spectrum is very different from the main endogenous absorbers (a sharp band peaking at 690–700 nm).
source: The fact that the iRFP720 absorption spectrum is very different from the main endogenous absorbers (a sharp band peaking at 690–700 nm, Figure 6—figure supplement 2) facilitated its detection even with minimal changes of photoacoustic intensity compared to the background.
evidence: This is demonstrated by spectral data shown in Figure 6—figure supplement 2.

claim: Multispectral processing of MSOT cross sections revealed the presence of tumours on the right shoulder, spinal cord, in the region dorsal of the kidney, back, hip, and right leg.
source: After scanning the animal in 1 mm steps, multispectral processing of the corresponding cross sections (Figure 6b) revealed the presence of tumours on the right shoulder (1), spinal cord (2), in the region dorsal of the kidney (2a and 2b), back (3), hip (4 and 5), and right leg (6).
evidence: This is observed in the MSOT imaging data shown in Figure 6b.

claim: Ex vivo luminescence imaging confirmed the observations made with in vivo photoacoustic tomography.
source: Ex vivo luminescence imaging confirmed the observations made with in vivo photoacoustic tomography (e.g. tumour masses 2a and 2b were found attached to the anterior-dorsal part of the kidneys) (Figure 6c).
evidence: This is demonstrated by ex vivo imaging data shown in Figure 6c that validates the in vivo MSOT findings.

claim: Expression of iRFP720 was confirmed by ex vivo fluorescence imaging of tumours.
source: Expression of iRFP720 was also confirmed by ex vivo fluorescence imaging of these tumours (Figure 6—figure supplement 3).
evidence: This is demonstrated by ex vivo fluorescence imaging data shown in Figure 6—figure supplement 3.

claim: Photoacoustic tomography using iRFP720 expression allowed precise longitudinal monitoring of tumour development from very early stages.
source: In addition to improving the anatomical localisation of internal tumours, photoacoustic tomography using iRFP720 expression also allowed precise longitudinal monitoring of tumour development from very early stages.
evidence: This is demonstrated by the longitudinal imaging data presented in the manuscript.

claim: The tumour mean diameter at day 13 was 1.2 mm.
source: The excellent spatial resolution enabled the localisation of this tumour in the vicinity of the pelvic ilium from day 13. The tumour mean diameter at this stage was 1.2 mm.
evidence: This is a measurement from MSOT imaging data.

claim: By day 19, 23 and 30, the tumour had expanded to 2.0, 2.2 and 3.3 mm, respectively.
source: By day 19, 23 and 30 it had expanded to 2.0, 2.2 and 3.3 mm, respectively.
evidence: These are measurements from longitudinal MSOT imaging data.

claim: Changes in the shape of the tumour were monitored from day 23 onwards when it branched off into two ramifications, which grew attached to the main part of the tumour.
source: Furthermore, changes in the shape of the tumour were also monitored from day 23 onwards when it branched off into two ramifications, which grew attached to the main part of the tumour (Figure 7 and Figure 7—video 1).
evidence: This is observed in the MSOT imaging data shown in Figure 7.

claim: GNRs were not used as contrast agents for tumour imaging, since the vast majority of them were cleared out following cell death.
source: Although GNRs were not used as contrast agents for tumour imaging, since the vast majority of them were cleared out following cell death, tumour growth was monitored with high spatial resolution via iRFP720 expression.
evidence: This is an observation from the longitudinal imaging studies.

claim: MSOT provides an excellent method to monitor tumour growth longitudinally from very early stages onwards (from sub mm size).
source: Overall, our analysis reveals that MSOT provides an excellent method to monitor tumour growth longitudinally from very early stages onwards (from sub mm size).
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the imaging data presented throughout the manuscript.

claim: Some tumours growing in very peripheral positions of the animal could not be monitored due to technical or procedural limitations of the MSOT imaging system.
source: Only some tumours growing in very peripheral positions of the animal could not be monitored due to technical or procedural limitations of the MSOT imaging system.
evidence: This is a limitation acknowledged by the authors based on their observations.

claim: The nose could not be imaged as it was placed in the nose cone for air and anaesthesia supply during the imaging process.
source: For example, the nose could not be imaged as it was placed in the nose cone for air and anaesthesia supply during the imaging process.
evidence: This is a technical limitation of the imaging setup.

claim: Any tumours in the lungs could not have been monitored with photoacoustic imaging due to a different sound propagation in air.
source: Any tumours in the lungs could not have been monitored with photoacoustic imaging due to a different sound propagation in air.
evidence: This is a fundamental limitation of photoacoustic imaging based on the physics of sound propagation.

claim: The presence of tumours in the lungs could be ruled out from the bioluminescence images.
source: However, the presence of tumours in the lungs could be ruled out from the bioluminescence images.
evidence: This is inferred from the bioluminescence imaging data.

claim: Multispectral optoacoustic tomography achieves high spatial resolution of the initial cell distribution through analysis of the GNR signal.
source: We show that multispectral optoacoustic tomography achieves high spatial resolution of the initial cell distribution through analysis of the GNR signal.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the imaging data presented in the manuscript.

claim: Expression of iRFP720 is initially undetectable due to the scattered distribution of cells.
source: Whilst expression of iRFP720 is initially undetectable, due to the scattered distribution of cells, it provides long-term tumour monitoring capability in MSOT as clustered iRFP720-positive cells lead to a stronger photoacoustic signal.
evidence: This is observed in the imaging data showing no iRFP720 signal immediately after injection but strong signal during tumour growth.

claim: Clustered iRFP720-positive cells lead to a stronger photoacoustic signal.
source: Whilst expression of iRFP720 is initially undetectable, due to the scattered distribution of cells, it provides long-term tumour monitoring capability in MSOT as clustered iRFP720-positive cells lead to a stronger photoacoustic signal.
evidence: This is inferred from the observation that iRFP720 becomes detectable when cells cluster into tumours.

claim: Bioluminescence imaging of luciferase allowed for the most sensitive detection of live cells for comparison and validation of the MSOT results.
source: Additionally, bioluminescence imaging of luciferase allowed for the most sensitive detection of live cells for comparison and validation of the MSOT results.
evidence: This is demonstrated throughout the manuscript where BLI and MSOT data are compared.

claim: The silica-coated GNRs provided the excellent photoacoustic sensitivity required to monitor the broad distribution of labelled cells shortly after systemic intra-cardiac injection.
source: The silica-coated GNRs provided the excellent photoacoustic sensitivity required to monitor the broad distribution of labelled cells shortly after systemic intra-cardiac injection.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the imaging data showing detection of cells immediately after injection.

claim: Because the GNRs maintained their optical signature when taken up by the cells, spectral unmixing could be applied in MSOT.
source: Because the GNRs maintained their optical signature when taken up by the cells, spectral unmixing could be applied in MSOT, which allowed GNR signals to be distinguished from other reporters (e.g. iRFP720) and endogenous absorbers, resulting in highly specific cell detection.
evidence: This is demonstrated by the spectral unmixing results shown throughout the manuscript.

claim: Spectral unmixing allowed GNR signals to be distinguished from other reporters (e.g. iRFP720) and endogenous absorbers, resulting in highly specific cell detection.
source: Because the GNRs maintained their optical signature when taken up by the cells, spectral unmixing could be applied in MSOT, which allowed GNR signals to be distinguished from other reporters (e.g. iRFP720) and endogenous absorbers, resulting in highly specific cell detection.
evidence: This is demonstrated by the spectral unmixing results and control experiments shown in the manuscript.

claim: Over the medium term (several days post-injection), photoacoustic GNR signals and luciferase bioluminescence signals became separated, indicating nanoparticle clearance and surviving cells, respectively.
source: Over the medium term, that is several days post-injection, photoacoustic GNR signals and luciferase bioluminescence signals became separated, indicating nanoparticle clearance and surviving cells, respectively.
evidence: This is observed in the longitudinal imaging data showing divergence of GNR and bioluminescence signals.

claim: The GNR signal became localized to the liver, which is in line with the known clearance pathway of nanoparticles and associated cell debris through the hepato-biliary system.
source: The GNR signal became localised to the liver, which is in line with the known clearance pathway of nanoparticles and associated cell debris through the hepato-biliary system.
evidence: This is observed in the imaging data and is consistent with known nanoparticle clearance mechanisms.

claim: Longitudinal monitoring of surviving cells and tumour formation was achieved via luciferase bioluminescence and iRFP720 photoacoustic tomography using the genetic reporters.
source: Using the genetic reporters, longitudinal monitoring of surviving cells and tumour formation was achieved via luciferase bioluminescence and iRFP720 photoacoustic tomography.
evidence: This is demonstrated by the longitudinal imaging data presented in the manuscript.

claim: Compared to other optical-based imaging technologies, the superior deep-tissue spatial resolution of MSOT provided precise information about anatomical localisation and morphology of tumours from very early stages (<1 mm diameter).
source: Compared to other optical-based imaging technologies, the superior deep-tissue spatial resolution of MSOT provided precise information about anatomical localisation and morphology of tumours from very early stages (<1 mm diameter).
evidence: This is demonstrated by the MSOT imaging data showing detection and characterization of small tumours.

claim: The optimal window for in vivo optical imaging lies in the near infrared (NIR) spectrum (~650–900 nm), since absorption through the main endogenous chromophores (oxy-haemoglobin, deoxy-haemoglobin, melanin, water and lipids) are minimal in this spectral range.
source: The optimal window for in vivo optical imaging lies in the near infrared (NIR) spectrum (~650–900 nm), since absorption through the main endogenous chromophores (oxy-haemoglobin, deoxy-haemoglobin, melanin, water and lipids) are minimal in this spectral range (Weber et al., 2016).
evidence: This is established knowledge in the field supported by citation.

claim: Firefly luciferase has become the most widely used reporter as its substrates, D-luciferin or CycLuc1, are very well tolerated by animals.
source: Firefly, luciferase has become the most widely used reporter as its substrates, D-luciferin or CycLuc1 (Evans et al., 2014), are very well tolerated by animals and, compared to other luciferases, its peak light emission at around 562 nm is closest to the infrared window for in vivo imaging (de Almeida et al., 2011).
evidence: This is established knowledge in the field supported by citations.

claim: Compared to other luciferases, firefly luciferase peak light emission at around 562 nm is closest to the infrared window for in vivo imaging.
source: Firefly, luciferase has become the most widely used reporter as its substrates, D-luciferin or CycLuc1 (Evans et al., 2014), are very well tolerated by animals and, compared to other luciferases, its peak light emission at around 562 nm is closest to the infrared window for in vivo imaging (de Almeida et al., 2011).
evidence: This is established knowledge in the field supported by citations.

claim: Acoustic scattering is three orders of magnitude less than photon scattering.
source: In fact, acoustic scattering is three orders of magnitude less than photon scattering (Wang and Hu, 2012), which overcomes deep tissue spatial resolution drawbacks of other optical-based imaging technologies.
evidence: This is established knowledge in the field supported by citation.

claim: Some iRFPs, such as iRFP720, have an absorption profile in the NIR window, thus enabling their use as reporter genes for photoacoustic imaging.
source: Interestingly, some iRFPs, such as iRFP720, have an absorption profile in the NIR window, thus enabling their use as reporter genes for photoacoustic imaging, and allowing deep tissue imaging and tumour monitoring in mice (Deliolanis et al., 2014; Jiguet-Jiglaire et al., 2014).
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by citations.

claim: New iRFPs have been proven to be useful genetic photoacoustic reporters in mammary gland and brain tumour monitoring.
source: For example, new iRFPs have been proven to be useful genetic photoacoustic reporters in mammary gland and brain tumour monitoring, which establishes them as dual-modality imaging probes (Deliolanis et al., 2014; Filonov et al., 2012; Krumholz et al., 2014).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: GNRs have extinction coefficients in the range of 4–5.5 × 10^9 M^−1cm^−1 for longitudinal surface plasmon between 728 and 845 nm.
